note: W7. Hand-computed. `outcome` is one of none | malformed | parsed — three and not two, because "this report proposed nothing" and "this report proposed something I could not read" are different facts and a screen that collapses them lies to whoever mistyped a brace. When `outcome` is `malformed`, `reason` is the exact string the parser reports. The LAST block that parses wins: the export prints the schema as a worked example in §9, so a user who pastes the document instead of the report hands this parser a block, and a conversation may carry a draft the model then corrected. That example's `weekStart` is the literal YYYY-MM-DD, which is why the `the export pasted back into itself` case is malformed rather than applied. A `weekStart` is round-tripped through `ISODate.dayNumber`, so a day that does not exist in its month (2026-02-30, 2026-02-29) is refused rather than silently normalised into March — and 2028-02-29, which does exist, is not. Numbers are bounded above as well as below: the block is model-authored, and `Int.init(Double)` TRAPS rather than throwing. The literal `YYYY-MM-DD` is the SCHEMA announcing itself and reads as `none`, so pasting the export instead of the reply is quietly "no targets in this report" rather than a red banner saying the model answered badly; `2026-02-30` is still `malformed`, because that one is a mistake. An empty fence is `none` in both of its spellings — closed and unterminated — which they did not used to agree on. The trailing-comma case records what Foundation's decoder ACTUALLY does (it accepts one) rather than what JSON says; leniency is the right side to err on here, and a fixture that guessed the other way would have been a test of nothing.
